research.text:
**RECOMMENDED**: Ski Niseko United on Thursday, January 14, **provided that** morning operations confirm upper-mountain lifts and avalanche gates will reopen following two days of wind holds.

### The Opportunity: Post-Storm Reopening
Snowfall recaps will highlight Wednesday’s 12-inch storm total at Niseko [evidence], but Wednesday is high risk: 55 mph westerly gusts [evidence] following Tuesday’s wind holds [evidence] will almost certainly keep upper chairs and peak gates closed, cramming resort traffic onto wind-scoured lower slopes. 

The premier opportunity is **Thursday at Niseko**. Winds drop dramatically to 22 mph [evidence], accompanied by 5 inches of new snow [evidence]. Because the upper mountain was shuttered Tuesday and likely Wednesday [evidence], 16+ inches of storm snow will have accumulated untouched in the upper bowls [evidence]. When patrol drops the ropes, expert skiers get deep, untracked steeps directly out the door of their lodging—fully covered by their Ikon Pass with zero driving required.

### Strongest Practical Alternative
The main competitor is **Wednesday at Rusutsu**. Forecast westerly gusts there are far milder at 28 mph [evidence], and its lower-elevation ridgelines reliably buffer high winds. With 9 inches of fresh snow [evidence], Rusutsu offers guaranteed, high-quality tree skiing on West and East Mountains. 

However, Rusutsu is partnered with the Epic Pass, not Ikon; skiing there requires purchasing an out-of-pocket day pass (regularly ¥11,500–¥14,500+) and navigating a 40- to 50-minute drive across snowy mountain passes. While the traveler’s budget can easily absorb the ticket cost, Rusutsu’s mellow fall lines cater more to cruisy trees than the steep, deep terrain this expert prefers.

### What Changes the Plan
Monitor Niseko United lift status and the Niseko Avalanche Information report early Thursday morning:
* **Stick to Thursday at Niseko** if the upper lifts (such as Grand Hirafu’s King Lift #4 or the Annupuri summit chairs) and backcountry gates are scheduled to spin.
* **Pivot to Wednesday at Rusutsu** if Wednesday morning weather reports show Niseko completely locked down and Thursday forecasts trend worse (e.g., wind holds continuing, high avalanche danger locking gates all day). In that scenario, buying a Rusutsu ticket is worth the expense to secure sheltered, wind-protected powder turns.
